heath_proof: Let there be two pyramids of the same height which have the triangular bases ABC, DEF, and vertices the points G, H, and let each of them be divided into two pyramids equal to one another and similar to the whole and into two equal prisms; [XII. 3] I say that, as the base ABC is to the base DEF, so are all the prisms in the pyramid ABCG to all the prisms, being equal in multitude, in the pyramid DEFH, For, since BO is equal to OC, and AL to LC, therefore LO is parallel to AB, and the triangle ABC is similar to the triangle LOC. For the same reason the triangle DEF is also similar to the triangle RVF. And, since BC is double of CO, and EF of FV, therefore, as BC is to CO, so is EF to FV. And on BC, CO are described the similar and similarly situated rectilineal figures ABC, LOC, and on EF, FV the similar and similarly situated figures DEF, RVF; therefore, as the triangle ABC is to the triangle LOC, so is the triangle DEF to the triangle RVF; [VI. 22] therefore, alternately, as the triangle ABC is to the triangle DEF, so is the triangle LOC to the triangle RVF. [V. 16] But, as the triangle LOC is to the triangle RVF, so is the prism in which the triangle LOC is the base and PMN its opposite to the prism in which the triangle RVF is the base and STU its opposite; [Lemma following]therefore also, as the triangle ABC is to the triangle DEF, so is the prism in which the triangle LOC is the base and PMN its opposite to the prism in which the triangle RVF is the base and STU its opposite. But, as the said prisms are to one another, so is the prism in which the parallelogram KBOL is the base and the straight line PM its opposite to the prism in which the parallelogram QEVR is the base and the straight line ST its opposite. [XI. 39; cf. XII. 3] Therefore also the two prisms, that in which the parallelogram KBOL is the base and PM its opposite, and that in which the triangle LOC is the base and PMN its opposite, are to the prisms in which QEVR is the base and the straight line ST its opposite and in which the triangle RVF is the base and STU its opposite in the same ratio [V. 12] Therefore also, as the base ABC is to the base DEF, so are the said two prisms to the said two prisms. And similarly, if the pyramids PMNG, STUH be divided into two prisms and two pyramids, as the base PMN is to the base STU, so will the two prisms in the pyramid PMNG be to the two prisms in the pyramid STUH. But, as the base PMN is to the base STU, so is the base ABC to the base DEF; for the triangles PMN, STU are equal to the triangles LOC, RVF respectively. Therefore also, as the base ABC is to the base DEF, so are the four prisms to the four prisms. And similarly also, if we divide the remaining pyramids into two pyramids and into two prisms, then, as the base ABC is to the base DEF, so will all the prisms in the pyramid ABCG be to all the prisms, being equal in multitude, in the pyramid DEFH.

12.4
**Statement:** If there be two pyramids of the same height which have triangular bases, and cach of them be divided into two pyramids equal to one another and similar to the whole, and into two equal prisms, then, as the base of the one pyramid is to the base of the other pyramid, so will all the prisms in the one pyramid be to all the prisms, being equal in multitude, in the other pyramid.

**Statement:** If there be two pyramids of the same height which have triangular bases, and each of them be divided into two pyramids equal to one another and similar to the whole, and into two equal prisms, then, as the base of the one pyramid is to the base of the other pyramid, so will all the prisms in the one pyramid be to all the prisms, being equal in multitude, in the other pyramid.

**Step 1.** Let ABCG and DEFH be two pyramids of the same height, having the triangular bases ABC, DEF and the vertices G, H. From G and H let GZ and HZ' be drawn perpendicular to the planes ABC and DEF respectively (11.11); these perpendiculars are the heights of the pyramids (D6.4), so that by hypothesis GZ = HZ'. Divide each pyramid as in 12.3. In ABCG bisect AB, BC, CA at K, O, L and GA, GB, GC at P, M, N; then ABCG is divided into the two pyramids AKLP and GPMN, equal to one another and similar to the whole, and into two equal prisms, namely the prism I whose base is the parallelogram KBOL and whose opposite edge is PM, and the prism II whose base is the triangle LOC and whose opposite face is the triangle PMN (12.3). Likewise in DEFH bisect DE, EF, FD at Q, V, R and HD, HE, HF at S, T, U; then DEFH is divided into two pyramids and into two equal prisms, the prism I' with base the parallelogram QEVR and opposite edge ST, and the prism II' with base the triangle RVF and opposite face the triangle STU (12.3). I say that, as the base ABC is to the base DEF, so are the prisms I and II together to the prisms I' and II' together.

**Step 2.** Since CL = LA and CO = OB, the ratios CL : LA and CO : OB are each the ratio of a magnitude to an equal magnitude and are therefore the same ratio (D5.5); thus the sides CA, CB of the triangle ABC are cut proportionally at L and O, and LO is parallel to AB (6.2). For the same reason RV is parallel to DE.

**Step 3.** Since LO is parallel to AB, the angle CLO is equal to the angle CAB and the angle COL to the angle CBA (1.29), and the angle at C is common; so the triangle LOC is equiangular with the triangle ABC, and the sides about the equal angles are proportional (6.4). Therefore the triangle LOC is similar to the triangle ABC (D6.1), C corresponding to C, O to B and L to A, so that LOC and ABC are similarly described upon CO and CB. In the same way the triangle RVF is similar to the triangle DEF and similarly described upon FV and FE.

**Step 4.** BC is double of CO, and EF is double of FV. Since parts have the same ratio as the same multiples of them taken in corresponding order, CO : FV = BC : EF (5.15); and alternately CO : BC = FV : EF (5.16).

**Step 5.** The four straight lines CO, BC, FV, EF are thus proportional; on CO and BC are described the similar and similarly situated triangles LOC and ABC, and on FV and EF the similar and similarly situated triangles RVF and DEF. Therefore triangle LOC : triangle ABC = triangle RVF : triangle DEF (6.22), and alternately triangle LOC : triangle RVF = triangle ABC : triangle DEF (5.16).

**Step 6.** [Lemma: the prisms II and II' are to one another as the triangles LOC and RVF.] First, the prisms II and II' are of the same height. The triangles LOC and PMN are the two opposite faces of the prism II, so the plane PMN is parallel to the plane ABC (D11.13). The two straight lines GC and GZ drawn from G are cut by the parallel planes PMN and ABC, GC at N and C, and GZ at the point Y in which it meets the plane PMN and at Z; therefore GN : NC = GY : YZ (11.17). But GN = NC; therefore GY = YZ (D5.5). Hence YZ, the perpendicular from the point Y of the face PMN to the plane ABC, which is the height of the prism II, is half of GZ. In the same way the height Y'Z' of the prism II', cut off from HZ' by the plane STU, is half of HZ'. Since GZ = HZ', their halves YZ and Y'Z' are equal; so the prisms II and II' are of the same height.

**Step 7.** Through L draw LX parallel to CO and through O draw OX parallel to CL (1.31), meeting at X, so that LCOX is a parallelogram; and in the plane PMN draw PX' parallel to NM and MX' parallel to NP (1.31), meeting at X', so that PNMX' is a parallelogram. This completes the parallelepipedal solid LCOX-PNMX', which has the parallelogram LCOX in the plane ABC as base and PNMX' in the parallel plane PMN as opposite face, and is therefore of the same height YZ as the prism II. The plane PMOL passes through the diagonals LO and PM of the opposite faces LCOX and PNMX'; therefore it bisects the solid (11.28), and the prism II, being one of the two halves, is half of the solid, so that the solid is double of the prism II. Similarly complete the parallelepipedal solid RFVW-SUTW' upon the prism II', of height Y'Z', which is bisected by the plane STVR, so that it is double of the prism II'.

**Step 8.** Parallelepipedal solids which are of the same height are to one another as their bases (11.32); therefore solid LCOX-PNMX' : solid RFVW-SUTW' = parallelogram LCOX : parallelogram RFVW.

**Step 9.** The parallelogram LCOX is bisected by its diameter LO (1.34) and is therefore double of the triangle LOC; likewise the parallelogram RFVW is double of the triangle RVF. Hence triangle LOC : triangle RVF = parallelogram LCOX : parallelogram RFVW (5.15). Again, since the solids are doubles of the prisms II and II' (Step 7), prism II : prism II' = solid LCOX-PNMX' : solid RFVW-SUTW' (5.15). Therefore prism II : prism II' = parallelogram LCOX : parallelogram RFVW = triangle LOC : triangle RVF (5.11), which proves the lemma.

**Step 10.** From Steps 5 and 9, triangle ABC : triangle DEF = triangle LOC : triangle RVF = prism II : prism II' (5.11).

**Step 11.** The prism I is equal to the prism II, and the prism I' to the prism II' (12.3). Equal magnitudes have the same ratio to the same, and the same has the same ratio to equal magnitudes (5.7); hence prism I : prism II' = prism II : prism II', and prism I : prism I' = prism I : prism II'; therefore prism I : prism I' = prism II : prism II' (5.11).

**Step 12.** Thus prism II : prism II' = prism I : prism I' (Step 11); and since these magnitudes are proportional, as one of the antecedents is to one of the consequents, so are all the antecedents to all the consequents (5.12): (prism II together with prism I) : (prism II' together with prism I') = prism II : prism II' = triangle ABC : triangle DEF (Step 10, 5.11). Therefore, as the base ABC is to the base DEF, so are all the prisms in the pyramid ABCG to all the prisms, equal in multitude, in the pyramid DEFH. Q.E.D.

*Path note:* The bases ABC, DEF could instead be compared by showing that each is quadruple of the triangle LOC or RVF cut off by the bisection (via 1.33, 1.34 and 5.15); the route through 6.22 uses the similarity already obtained from the bisection and is the more direct. The bisection of the perpendicular GZ by the plane PMN is taken from 11.17; it could equally be derived from 11.16 together with 6.2 in the plane GCZ.
